newsitem.title: USA: NAPM index rises for 10th month in a row.
newsitem.headline: NAPM index rises for 10th month in a row.

text.p: U.S. manufacturing activity grew in November for a 10th consecutive month, with surprisingly strong gains in production and new orders, the nation's purchasing executives said Monday.

The National Association of Purchasing Management said its index rose to 52.7 percent in November from 50.2 percent in October. It was the seventh time in the past eight months that the index was above 50 percent, which signals manufacturing growth, while a reading below that level indicates contraction.

"The manufacturing sector grew more rapidly in November than in October with production and new orders indicating faster rates of growth," said Ralph Kauffman, chairman of the group's Business Survey Committee.
"However, this was tempered with a faster rate of decrease in prices paid, and continued reductions in employment, inventories, and backlog of orders."
Purchasing executives, who buy supplies for the nation's manufacturing plants, were "somewhat more bullish" about business conditions than in October, the group said.
NAPM's production index rose for an eighth consecutive month, to 58.6 percent from 56.6 percent in October. The rate was the highest since January 1995, when it hit 59.9 percent.
The new orders index gained 3.8 points to 55.4 percent. The backlog of orders fell for the fifth month in November, to 49.0 percent.
NAPM's supplier deliveries index moved up to 51.5 percent in November, as deliveries slowed from 50.7 percent in October.
Manufacturing jobs decreased for the 22nd consecutive month, with index rising to 47.5 percent in November from 45.5 percent in October, the group said.
NAPM's price index eased to 45.9 percent from 47.1 percent in October as prices paid fell for a second month in a row. The inventories index rose to 41.8 percent from 38.9 percent in October.

NAPM's new export orders index eased for the third straight month, to 55.8 percent from 56.1 percent in October. But the index remained above 50 percent for the ninth month in a row, indicating an increase in export orders.
Imports of materials by manufacturers increased for the fifth month, but also at a slower rate as NAPM's imports index slid to 52.5 percent from 53.8 percent in October.

Industries with the highest production growth rates were furniture; apparel; rubber & plastic products; chemicals; wood and wood products; electronic components and equipment; instruments and photographic equipment; printing and publishing; and industrial and commercial equipment and computers.
